en: Virgin coconut oil from Quezon turns from a clear liquid to a solid white fat when the room temperature drops below 24 degrees Celsius.
The iron railings along Manila Bay undergo a chemical change called rusting when exposed to the salty, humid sea air.
A bowl of halo-halo is a heterogeneous mixture because you can easily see and separate its distinct ingredients like ube halaya and sweet beans.
When you stir brown sugar into a glass of cold calamansi juice, it dissolves to form a uniform liquid solution.
Salt farmers in Dasol, Pangasinan, use the sun's heat to evaporate seawater, leaving behind solid salt crystals in a physical change.
Fermenting shrimp to make bagoong alamang in Bulacan is a chemical change that produces new substances with different smells and tastes.
Abaca fibers from the Bicol region have high tensile strength, making them an excellent solid material for manufacturing durable ship ropes.
Mayon Volcano in Albay releases sulfur dioxide gas during eruptions, demonstrating that gases expand to fill the space in the atmosphere.
Making kesong puti from carabao milk in Laguna involves adding vinegar to separate the solid curds from the liquid whey in a mixture.
Water droplets form on the outside of a cold buko juice bottle in Manila due to the condensation of water vapor in the humid air.
Burning dried rice straw in Nueva Ecija fields after harvest is a chemical change that produces ash, heat, and smoke.
Copper mined in Benguet is an excellent electrical conductor, which is why it is widely used to make wires for Philippine homes.
